title: Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents
title_zh: Mem++：面向长期组织型 LLM 智能体的非破坏性记忆

paragraphs.en: Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, where many authors record decisions across documents over months. Because a revised decision arrives as a new document rather than an edit, answering a question requires knowing which version held at a given time. However, most memory systems compress the record at write time. By distilling each document into facts, notes or graph edges, these methods fix what can be answered before any question is asked. To address this, we propose Mem++, a non-destructive memory framework shifting from write-time distillation to read-time selection. Mem++ stores every document whole with its date and author, and it calls no generative model at write time. At read time, it retrieves only documents dated up to the time a question asks about and fuses lexical and semantic rankings. Unlike systems that overwrite older versions, Mem++ keeps them and leaves the choice to the answering model. Evaluations on the organizational benchmark OrgMemBench demonstrate that Mem++ surpasses the strongest memory system baseline by 8.0 to 13.1 points across two answering models. With gpt-4.1-mini, it also achieves the best overall score, 2.6 points above RAG. In addition, Mem++ achieves the best average LLM-judge score on LoCoMo and ranks second on LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} , behind only its entity-graph variant. Code for benchmark evaluation is available at https://github.com/AIDAChip-Inc/mem-plus-plus

paragraphs.en: Large Language Model (LLM) agents now take part in organizational work, from daily tasks to decisions that span many teams over months ( Kirchdorfer et al., 2026 ) . Such critical work is only possible if the agent can correctly recall what was already decided ( Zeng et al., 2025 ) . In an organization, the record of past decisions is shared; organizational memory keeps the history that informs present decisions ( Walsh and Ungson, 1991 ) , and it is written by humans and agents alike. To have a deeper understanding of the context and intent of the organization, a shared memory that mixes agents, humans, and compound their knowledge becomes a necessity.

paragraphs.en: Organizational memory differs from the conversational, single-agent memory that existing systems were built for ( Figure 1 ). Conversational memory has a single dialogue whose statements accumulate rather than compete, and a later statement is therefore read as an update of an earlier one. Organizational memory, in contrast, is written by many people independently of one another across email, tickets, meeting notes and shared documents ( Gardner, 2026 ) . Moreover, a decision that changes an earlier one is written as a new document rather than as an edit to the old one. For example, a policy set in March, revised in June and reversed in September exists as three documents, and all three remain because nobody goes back to remove them. Consequently, answering a question against this record takes more than finding the most recent version. Conversational memory struggles here, because they treat every statement as coming from the same authority. For example, Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) resolves the conflict by overwriting, so the approved decision is replaced by the proposal and can no longer be retrieved afterwards. In addition, Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) keeps both statements, because its Graphiti engine stamps every edge with the valid period, but it stores extracted facts rather than the documents.

paragraphs.en: Existing memory systems resolve one trade-off at ingest, between keeping the record and structuring it. Traditional retrieval-based systems keep the raw text and search it by similarity ( Packer et al., 2023 ) , and nothing is discarded, but nothing is organized either. A query, therefore, cannot distinguish a superseded value from one still in force. This is how the memory stream of generative agents works, appending each observation in its original form and retrieving it later by relevance and recency ( Park et al., 2023 ) . Structured systems make the opposite choice. They record how statements relate to one another at ingest, and the raw text does not survive that step. For instance, Mem0 stores a set of facts ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , Zep a graph of dated edges ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) , and HippoRAG and GraphRAG an entity graph extracted from the corpus ( Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ; Edge et al., 2024 ) , and in none of them does a later query reach the document itself. A memo that changes a decision is reduced to a relation between an entity and a value. Its reason, condition and approval are not entity-shaped, and they never enter the store. What will be answerable is therefore fixed before any question has been asked. As we show in Section 4 , this explains the sharp drop of conversational memory systems on OrgMemBench, a benchmark of multi-author temporal, contradiction and justification-chain questions that define organizational memory.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的记忆系统在摄入阶段解决了一种权衡：在保留记录与结构化记录之间做出选择。 传统的检索式系统会保留原始文本，并通过相似性进行检索（Packer 等，2023），虽然不会丢弃任何内容，但同样也没有对内容进行组织。 因此，查询无法区分已被取代的值与仍然有效的值。 生成式智能体的记忆流正是如此运作：每次观察都以原始形式追加进去，之后通过相关性和时效性进行检索（Park 等，2023）。 结构化系统则做出了相反的选择。 它们在摄入阶段就记录了陈述之间的相互关系，而原始文本在这一步骤中并不会被保留下来。 例如，Mem0 存储一组事实（Chhikara 等，2025），Zep 存储一个带有日期标记的边构成的图（Rasmussen 等，2025），HippoRAG 和 GraphRAG 则存储从语料库中提取出的实体图（Gutiérrez 等，2024；Edge 等，2024）；在这些系统中，后续的查询都无法直接访问文档本身。 一个改变决策的备忘录会被简化为实体与值之间的关系。 其理由、条件和批准过程并不具备实体的形态，因此也从未被存入存储系统。 因此，在提出任何问题之前，谁需要负责就已经被固定下来了。 正如我们在第 4 节中所示，这解释了对话式记忆系统在 OrgMemBench 上的表现为何急剧下降——该基准测试专门评估多作者、涉及时间性、矛盾性和论证链的问题，这些正是组织记忆的核心特征。

paragraphs.en: To address these limitations we introduce Mem++ , an organizational memory architecture that moves the decision about what matters from write time to read time. (i) Every artifact is stored whole and remains the unit of retrieval. (ii) Structure can be added as an optional layer over the retained documents rather than as a replacement for them. A Mem++ pass groups near-duplicates and marks older conflicting versions as superseded without deleting them, and we evaluate it as an ablation. (iii) Selection is deferred until a question arrives, and it therefore ranges over the full record rather than a pruned set of facts. What distinguishes Mem++ is therefore not that the record is kept, but that each document stays whole with its date and the choice between versions is made at read time. Our contributions are as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了 Mem++——一种组织记忆架构，它将“哪些内容重要”的决策从写入时转移到了读取时。 (i) 每个产物都以完整形式存储，并始终作为检索的基本单位。 (ii) 结构可以作为可选层叠加在保留的文档之上，而非取代它们。 Mem++ 处理流程会将近重复项进行分组，并将较旧的冲突版本标记为过时，但不会删除它们；我们将此作为消融研究进行评估。 (iii) 选择过程会延迟到问题出现时才开始，因此其范围覆盖完整记录，而非一个经过裁剪的事实集合。 因此，Mem++ 的独特之处并不在于记录被保留下来，而在于每份文档都保持完整并附带其日期，版本间的选择则在读取时做出。 我们的贡献如下：

paragraphs.en: Agent memories give an LLM persistent state beyond its context window, differing in how they carry information across sessions. MemGPT ( Packer et al., 2023 ) and the generative agents memory ( Park et al., 2023 ) hold the record in full and leave every judgement to retrieval. Details survives, but nothing marks how one statement stands to another, so a query cannot separate a replaced value from one still activated. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds answers in an external corpus by chunking documents, embedding them, and returning the nearest chunks at query time ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Karpukhin et al., 2020 ) . However, the words survive while the document does not, since chunking separates a passage from the rest of its text and from any later version of it. Most recent approaches instead compress at ingest, gaining structure at the cost of the record. Mem0 distils each document into facts and overwrites them on conflict ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) . Similarly, A-Mem, Nemori, LightMem and LiCoMemory rewrite interactions into episodes through clustering, summarization or note-taking ( Xu et al., 2026 ; Nan et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . In addition, G-Memory organizes these episodes hierarchically ( Zhang et al., 2026 ) , PREMem reasons as it writes ( Kim et al., 2025 ) , and MemOS exposes memory as a managed layer ( Li et al., 2025 ) . Each gains a compact store but loses the source and the links between its statements, and what can be answered is fixed at ingest. In contrast, Mem++ stores every document whole at write time and marks superseded statements with a date instead of deleting them. This approach keeps every version available and leaves the choice between them to read time, and conflicting statements from different authors therefore remain answerable.
paragraphs.zh: 智能体记忆为大型语言模型提供了超越其上下文窗口的持久状态，不同方法在跨会话携带信息的方式上存在差异。 MemGPT（Packer 等人，2023）和生成式智能体记忆（Park 等人，2023）完整保留记录，并将所有判断交由检索机制处理。 细节得以保留，但没有任何标记能说明某条陈述与其他陈述的关系，因此查询时无法区分被替换的值与仍生效的值。 检索增强生成（RAG）通过将文档分块、嵌入并在查询时返回最相关的分块，使答案以外部语料库为基础（Lewis 等人，2020；Karpukhin 等人，2020）。 然而，文字得以保留而文档本身却不存在了，因为分块会将一段文字与其文本中的其余部分以及任何后续版本分离。 大多数近期方法则选择在摄入阶段进行压缩，以牺牲记录完整性为代价换取结构化存储。 Mem0 将每份文档提炼为事实，并在发生冲突时覆盖这些事实（Chhikara 等人，2025）。 类似地，A-Mem、Nemori、LightMem 和 LiCoMemory 通过聚类、摘要或笔记记录，将交互过程重写为事件片段（Xu 等人，2026；Nan 等人，2025；Fang 等人，2026；Huang 等人，2026）。 此外，G-Memory 将这些事件片段进行层级组织（Zhang 等人，2026），PREMem 在写入时同步进行推理（Kim 等人，2025），而 MemOS 则将记忆暴露为一个受管理的层次（Li 等人，2025）。 这些方法虽然获得了紧凑的存储结构，但丢失了原始来源及其陈述间的关联，且可回答的内容在摄入阶段即已固定。 相比之下，Mem++ 在写入时完整保存每份文档，并用日期标记被替代的陈述，而非将其删除。 这种方法保留了所有可用版本，并将版本间的选择留到读取时决定，因此来自不同作者的冲突陈述仍然可以被回答。

paragraphs.en: Temporal questions ask what held at a given time or what a newer statement replaced, and conversational benchmarks such as LongMemEval and LoCoMo test them through knowledge-update and temporal-reasoning categories ( Wu et al., 2024 ; Maharana et al., 2024 ) . Existing systems handle such changes in two ways. The first discards or alters the older value. For instance, Mem0 overwrites an older fact once a newer one arrives ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) , A-Mem revises related notes in place when a new one is added ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , and MemoryBank lets older memories fade along a forgetting curve ( Zhong et al., 2024 ) . The second keeps the older value with a date. Zep and LongMemEval attach time intervals or timestamps to stored facts so that queries can be bounded by date ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) . In conversational memory, both mechanisms treat a change as one narrator updating their own facts, and the newest value is therefore assumed to be correct while the older one is removed or kept only as history. In an organization, however, changes arrive as new documents from different authors across different channels, and questions ask about past versions as often as about the current state ( Gardner, 2026 ) . Mem++ addresses this by keeping every version as a stored document, marking the replaced one with the date it stopped holding. Then, each retrieval is bounded by the date in the question, which lets one store answer what holds now, what held before, and what changed. In other terms, it reconstructs the life journey of a fact and how it changed. This is useful for organization to track pivot points in decisions making, allowing the agents and humans to revisit these later.
paragraphs.zh: 时间相关问题询问在特定时刻存在什么，或较新的陈述取代了旧的内容；而 LongMemEval 和 LoCoMo 等对话基准则通过知识更新和时间推理类别来测试这些问题（Wu 等人，2024；Maharana 等人，2024）。 现有系统以两种方式处理此类变化。 第一种方式是丢弃或修改旧值。 例如，Mem0 会在新事实到来时覆盖旧事实（Chhikara 等人，2025）；A-Mem 在添加新内容时会直接修订相关笔记（Xu 等人，2026）；而 MemoryBank 则让旧记忆沿遗忘曲线逐渐淡化（Zhong 等人，2024）。 第二种方式是保留旧值并附上日期。 Zep 和 LongMemEval 会将时间间隔或时间戳附加到存储的事实中，以便查询可以按日期限定范围（Rasmussen 等人，2025；Wu 等人，2024）。 在对话记忆中，这两种机制都将变化视为叙述者更新自身事实的行为，因此默认最新值为正确值，而旧值则被移除或仅保留为历史记录。 然而，在组织环境中，变化以不同作者通过不同渠道发送的新文档形式出现，而问题同样频繁地涉及过往版本而非当前状态（Gardner，2026）。 Mem++ 通过保留每个版本作为独立存储的文档来解决这一问题，并用停止生效的日期标记被取代的版本。 随后，每次检索都会根据问题中的日期限定范围，从而可以分别回答当前有效的事实、过去有效的事实以及发生变化的内容。 换言之，它重建了一个事实的生命历程及其变化过程。 这对组织而言很有用，因为它能追踪决策过程中的关键转折点，使智能体和人类能够日后重新审视这些节点。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate Mem++ on three benchmarks, one organizational and two conversational, which together cover the settings it is Mem++ designed for. OrgMemBench ( Gardner, 2026 ) is our primary benchmark, a synthetic bi-temporal corpus of one fictional organization that we use unmodified. We run its medium tier, which pairs 443 dated artifacts, organized into 157 threads over 18 months where later decisions revise earlier ones, with 73 questions over six capabilities that range from supersession to contradiction (Figure 3 ). The question count is small, yet each answer is graded against a rubric rather than marked right or wrong, giving 247 graded facets and a score in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] that reflects partial coverage of the expected evidence. LoCoMo ( Maharana et al., 2024 ) provides 10 multi-session dialogues of about 24K tokens each and 1,540 questions across four reasoning categories, and it is the most widely used for memories. LongMemEval S ( Wu et al., 2024 ) keeps a similar question format while spreading each of its 500 questions over roughly 48 sessions and 494 turns, which tests if a memory still holds when the history grows.

paragraphs.en: We benchmark against seven methods that range from no external memory to richly structured ones, namely Full Context (entire history in the prompt), RAG-4096 ( Lewis et al., 2020 , 4096-token chunks for dense retrieval) , Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 , fact extraction with update and delete rules) , Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 , temporal knowledge graph with dated edges) , A-Mem ( Xu et al., 2026 , structured notes with evolving links) , LangMem ( LangChain AI, 2025 , automatic memory extraction across sessions) , and gbrain ( Gardner, 2026 , entity graph over organizational documents) . Full Context, RAG-4096, Mem0 and Zep serve as general-purpose baselines and run on all three benchmarks, whereas A-Mem and LangMem, which designed for conversational memory, run only on LoCoMo and LongMemEval S , and gbrain, which was released with OrgMemBench, runs only there.
paragraphs.zh: 我们以七种方法作为基准进行比较，这些方法的外部记忆能力从完全无外部记忆到高度结构化不等，具体包括：Full Context（整个历史对话内容都包含在提示中）、RAG-4096（Lewis et al., 2020，使用 4096 个词元的分块进行密集检索）、Mem0（Chhikara et al., 2025，通过更新和删除规则提取事实）、Zep（Rasmussen et al., 2025，带有日期标记边的时序知识图谱）、A-Mem（Xu et al., 2026，包含动态链接的结构化笔记）、LangMem（LangChain AI, 2025，跨会话自动提取记忆）以及 gbrain（Gardner, 2026，基于组织文档的实体图谱）。 Full Context、RAG-4096、Mem0 和 Zep 作为通用基准方法，在所有三个基准测试中均运行；而专为对话记忆设计的 A-Mem 和 LangMem 仅在 LoCoMo 和 LongMemEval S 上运行，与 OrgMemBench 一同发布的 gbrain 则仅在该基准测试中运行。

paragraphs.en: On all three datasets, our primary evaluation metric is the LLM-judge score (abbreviated as LLM for simplicity), using gpt-4o-mini as the judges. For LongMemEval S , prompts are adapted to its task-specific question-answering format, following Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) . These metrics are accuracy metrics of different standard, and are scaled to the 0–100 range, with higher values indicating better performance and 100 denoting a perfect score.

paragraphs.en: To ensure fair comparison, Mem0 and Zep retrieve memory contexts, which are then fed to gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1-mini for answer generation. All other methods, including Mem++, employ the same models for answer generation, while Mem g ++ uses gpt-4o-mini as its internal graph backbone. All retrieval-based baselines employ the powerful text-embedding-3-small model, whereas Mem++ uses the lightweight all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model. The lexical index matches query terms disjunctively by default and conjunctively on OrgMemBench. Key hyperparameters are the fusion constant γ \gamma and the pathway weights w ℓ w_{\ell} , while the consolidation threshold τ \tau applies only when consolidation is enabled. For retrieval count, we fix k = 50 k=50 in main experiments, while k k varies from 10 to 100 in the ablation study, as shown in the Appendix.

paragraphs.en: Strong Performance on Organizational Memory. Mem++ achieves the best overall score on OrgMemBench with gpt-4.1-mini, reaching 57.6 and surpassing the strongest baseline, RAG, by 2.6 points. With gpt-4o-mini, Mem g ++ and Mem++ rank first and second with 44.4 and 44.2, ahead of RAG at 43.4. paragraphs.en: We have argued for a non-destructive view of organizational memory, where each document is kept whole rather than distilled at write time. Mem++ follows this view by keeping every version in one store and deferring the choice between versions to read time. Experiments show that this design outperforms write-time extraction on OrgMemBench, achieves the best average LLM-judge score on LoCoMo and remains competitive on LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} . Ablations further show that semantic retrieval over original documents drives these results, whereas consolidation, fact extraction and an entity graph add cost without a consistent gain. These findings suggest that keeping the original documents and choosing among them at read time is a strong baseline for organizational memory. we acknowledge that few public benchmarks target organizational memory, so our organizational evaluation rests on the 73 questions that OrgMemBench asks about one synthetic organization. In future work, we will collect more diverse organizational records and test Mem++ on them to improve the system in this setting.
paragraphs.zh: 我们主张一种非破坏性的组织记忆观，即每份文档在写入时都保持完整，而非被提炼。 Mem++ 遵循这一理念，将所有版本存储于单一存储单元中，并将版本间的选择推迟到读取时进行。 实验表明，该设计在 OrgMemBench 上的表现优于写入时提取方法，在 LoCoMo 上获得了 LLM 评审的最高平均分数，并且在 LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} 上仍具有竞争力。 消融实验进一步表明，对原始文档进行语义检索是取得这些结果的关键，而信息整合、事实提取和实体图则增加了成本，却未带来稳定的性能提升。 这些发现表明，保留原始文档并在读取时从中进行选择，是组织记忆的一个强大基线方法。我们承认目前很少有公开基准专门针对组织记忆，因此我们的组织评估基于 OrgMemBench 提出的关于一个合成组织的 73 个问题。 在未来的工作中，我们将收集更多样化的组织记录，并在此类数据上测试 Mem++，以进一步优化该系统。

sents.zh: 实验表明，该设计在 OrgMemBench 上的表现优于写入时提取方法，在 LoCoMo 上获得了 LLM 评审的最高平均分数，并且在 LongMemEval S {}_{\text{S}} 上仍具有竞争力。

sents.en: Ablations further show that semantic retrieval over original documents drives these results, whereas consolidation, fact extraction and an entity graph add cost without a consistent gain.
sents.zh: 消融实验进一步表明，对原始文档进行语义检索是取得这些结果的关键，而信息整合、事实提取和实体图则增加了成本，却未带来稳定的性能提升。

sents.en: These findings suggest that keeping the original documents and choosing among them at read time is a strong baseline for organizational memory. we acknowledge that few public benchmarks target organizational memory, so our organizational evaluation rests on the 73 questions that OrgMemBench asks about one synthetic organization.
sents.zh: 这些发现表明，保留原始文档并在读取时从中进行选择，是组织记忆的一个强大基线方法。我们承认目前很少有公开基准专门针对组织记忆，因此我们的组织评估基于 OrgMemBench 提出的关于一个合成组织的 73 个问题。

sents.en: In future work, we will collect more diverse organizational records and test Mem++ on them to improve the system in this setting.
sents.zh: 在未来的工作中，我们将收集更多样化的组织记录，并在此类数据上测试 Mem++，以进一步优化该系统。

paragraphs.en: where a conflict means one fact took a new value over time, a restatement means the rows say the same thing in different words, and distinct means the rows only look alike. In a conflict, the row with the latest event date stays current. Each older row keeps its text and date and is marked in σ \sigma as superseded by that row, and it therefore remains retrievable with its own date. paragraphs.en: Mem0 ( Chhikara et al., 2025 ) uses an LLM to extract salient facts from each new message and compares each fact with the most similar stored memories. An LLM then adds, updates or deletes a memory or leaves the store unchanged, so a newer fact can overwrite an older one.

paragraphs.en: Zep ( Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) builds a temporal knowledge graph with its Graphiti engine. It extracts entities and facts from each episode and stores each fact as an edge with the period over which it held. When a later fact contradicts an edge, Zep invalidates that edge. At query time it combines semantic, keyword and graph search over facts, entities and communities.
paragraphs.zh: Zep（Rasmussen 等，2025）使用其 Graphiti 引擎构建一个时序知识图谱。 它从每一集内容中提取实体和事实，并将每个事实存储为一条边，同时记录该事实成立的时间段。 当后续的事实与某条边矛盾时，Zep 会失效该边。 在查询时，它会结合语义、关键词以及对事实、实体和社群的图谱搜索。

paragraphs.en: Table 6 lists the retrieval settings that differ across benchmarks. All runs share the fusion constant γ = 60 \gamma=60 , k = 50 k=50 retrieved rows and three recency slots. A disjunctive lexical index returns rows that match any query term, whereas a conjunctive one returns only rows that contain every term. On OrgMemBench the encoder runs locally and embeds at most 256 word pieces of each document, while the stored text and the lexical index keep the full document. Only the 15 Audit Replay questions of OrgMemBench carry an as-of date, so the date bound applies only to them.
